bios.Pierre Fenech: Chief Executive Officer of the Institute of Tourism Studies (ITS) — his sole government role since April 2025. He is himself an ITS graduate, holding a Diploma in Hospitality Management from the Institute, followed by a B.Com (Hons) in Tourism from the University of Malta and an Executive MBA. He began his career in food and beverage, event and general management roles at establishments including the Bugibba Holiday Complex, The Coastline Hotel and Island Caterers; in 2008 he was appointed Director of Operations and Quality Assurance at Island Caterers, a post he held until November 2012, when he became General Manager of MKIC Ltd, the company running Montekristo Estates on behalf of Island Hotels Group. In March 2015 he was appointed CEO of the Mediterranean Conference Centre (MCC), and later also took on the CEO role at ITS, holding both positions concurrently for years — an arrangement local media dubbed him the tourism sector's "Super CEO" for. In March 2025, Tourism Minister Ian Borg did not renew his MCC contract; Nigel Vella was appointed to succeed him at the MCC from April 2025, and Fenech has continued solely as CEO of ITS since. He has faced two notable controversies: in 2019 he gave Labour MP Rosianne Cutajar a paid consultancy contract later described as a "phantom" job, since she was found to have done little to no work for the payment — a Standards Commissioner probe questioned the ethics of the arrangement but did not find Fenech personally at fault, since the tourism ministry's then permanent secretary, Anthony Gatt, had approved the related expenses (Gatt was subsequently removed from the post); and in 2021 he issued a direct order using ITS funds to architect Gilbert Bartolo, who was the brother of then-Tourism Minister Clayton Bartolo, saying he was not aware of the family relationship at the time.

bios.Dr Oliver de Gaetano: President of the Council for the Professions Complementary to Medicine (CPCM) since July 2022, the statutory body regulating 20 health care professions in Malta including physiotherapy, dietetics, occupational therapy, radiography and podiatry among others.
